title: Normalized frame models of a vector-bundle projective completion
statement: For every scheme S, rank parameter d, module F, presentation P [def-amb-vector-projective-presentation-data] and frame e of F on an affine V [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], there are polynomial algebra coordinates q for P(V), a graded coefficient isomorphism g from the recorded relative projective-space local algebra [def-nagata-relative-projective-space], and a Proj isomorphism b. The coordinates send X_0 to t, X_{i+1} to x(e_i), preserve all degrees, commute with the structural maps over V, and identify the first standard open with D_+(t).

source.place: Tags 01OA, 01OB, 01OE and 01NG; projective bundles and their standard affine charts

proof.text: Evaluate the frame on the actual standard free-module sections and transport from the restricted scheme to V. This gives a basis of F(V). Its product with the singleton basis of R gives a basis of R × F(V) with distinguished first vector (1,0). Apply the symmetric-algebra polynomial equivalence and the presentation equivalence. Degree one is the span of basis generators, and degree n is its nth power, proving the grading equivalence.

source.place: Tags 01OA, 01OB, 01OE and 01NG; projective bundles and their standard affine charts

proof.text: Use the canonical relative projective-space affine polynomial equivalence and the coefficient ring isomorphism V.topIso to produce g and its inverse. Proj.map composition and identity show their scheme maps are inverse. On the whole affine base the relative-Proj embedding is an isomorphism; compose to get b. Naturality of the degree-zero Proj map proves the equation over V, and the preimage of a Proj basic open proves the standard-open equation.
